Autumn Scenery Reflected In Water Droplets

LIKE THIS MODEL? GIVE A ❤️

Model Introduction

  • The model has excellent generalization ability, adaptable to various autumn scenes such as nature and urban areas, and has a wide range of applications.

Base Prompt:Autumn scenery reflected in water droplets

The red keywords serve as the base prompt​​, followed by character or scene descriptions, which can be expressed in either tag-based language or natural language.

Overview

Step into a world where rain becomes poetry – where every droplet tells a story, every wet surface mirrors the sky, and the world is wrapped in a veil of gentle water. This LoRA captures the essence of atmospheric rainfall for Z Image Turbo: soft showers on quiet streets, rain-streaked windows offering blurred views, puddles reflecting distant lights, and the timeless beauty of wet landscapes. Whether you seek peaceful solitude, urban melancholy, or the raw power of a storm, this model delivers rain in all its forms – from delicate drizzle to dramatic downpour.

While other models focus on specific emotions or scenarios, "V67 Rain effect" is a versatile rain toolkit: a foundational LoRA that adds realistic, cinematic rainfall to any scene, enhancing atmosphere without overwhelming the subject.

Base Model

Z Image Turbo (also compatible with Flux and Ernie)

rain effect, wet atmosphere, soft rainfall

Why Z Image Turbo + V67 Rain effect?

Z Image Turbo excels at wet surfaces, atmospheric lighting, and soft fog – exactly what realistic rain effects need. The combination produces images with immersive depth: you can almost feel the cool rain on your skin, hear the rhythmic patter on rooftops, and see the world reflected in countless shimmering puddles.

Prompting Tips for Best Results

✅ Do this:

  • Start with rain effect, wet atmosphere

  • Add specific rain keywords: soft rainfall, heavy downpour, steady rain, light drizzle

  • Specify wet surfaces: wet asphalt, glass streaks, leaf droplets, puddle reflections

  • Use atmospheric cues: misty atmosphere, gentle fog, stormy sky

  • Keep colours desaturated with warm accents where needed

  • Specify time of day: dusk, dawn, overcast afternoon, blue hour

❌ Avoid:

  • Bright sunshine, saturated colours

  • Crowded scenes (unless specific)

  • Happy expressions, smiling people (if melancholy is desired)

  • Overloading with too many subjects

  • Forgetting to specify surface type for reflections

What This LoRA Excels At

✅ Gentle rain on quiet streets and windows
✅ Heavy downpour with visible rain streaks
✅ Wet surfaces – asphalt, cobblestones, glass, metal
✅ Puddle reflections with blurred mirrored worlds
✅ Rain-streaked windows with blurred exterior views
✅ Still lakes, ponds, and rivers with rain ripples
✅ Soft fog and mist that create depth and ethereal quality
✅ Desaturated blue-grey and warm sepia palettes
✅ Urban landscapes – cities, streets, architecture
✅ Natural landscapes – forests, moors, gardens, lakes
✅ Vehicles in the rain – trams, trains, vintage cars, boats
✅ Still life – flowers, books, objects, interiors
✅ Solitary figures – umbrella, silhouettes, contemplative
✅ Timeless atmosphere – old bridges, cobblestone streets, vintage aesthetics
✅ Cinematic rain across all contexts

What This LoRA Does NOT Excel At

❌ Extreme weather (hurricanes, floods) – this is atmospheric rain, not disaster
❌ Rain in brightly lit sunny scenes – rain implies overcast or low light
❌ Neon-drenched cyberpunk (unless combined with other models) – this is more naturalistic
❌ Heavy action scenes – rain here is contemplative, not chaotic

Limitations & Notes for Z Image Turbo

⚠️ Face expressions can sometimes lack emotion – use cinematic portrait or close-up for better results, or keep figures from behind or in silhouette for maximum atmospheric effect.

⚠️ Very complex scenes with multiple subjects may dilute the rain effect – keep to 1–3 key elements.

⚠️ Colour guidance is important – specify desaturated, muted tones, or warm sepia undertones if results are too vivid.

⚠️ Rain intensity can be controlled with keywords: soft rainfall, gentle rain, steady rain, heavy downpour, light drizzle.

⚠️ Surface specification helps: use wet asphalt, glass streaks, leaf droplets, puddle reflections to guide where rain appears.

⚠️ Negative prompt is crucial – always exclude bright, sunny, vibrant to maintain realistic rain atmosphere.

Troubleshooting Common Issues

Credits & Philosophy

Rain is not just weather – it is atmosphere, emotion, and poetry. This LoRA celebrates the beauty of water in all its forms: the gentle rhythm on rooftops, the distorted reflections in puddles, the cool mist on skin, the shimmer of wet leaves in grey light.

Inspired by:

  • The photography of Saul Leiter (rain on glass, blurred city views)

  • The cinema of Wong Kar-wai (rain as emotion, colour, mood)

  • The landscapes of Caspar David Friedrich (nature in stillness)

  • The quiet poetry of Japanese wabi-sabi aesthetics

Prompting Tips for Best Results

✅ Do This:

  • Start with (Macro:1.1) for strongest style adherence

  • Include the full trigger string to activate all macro elements

  • Specify the subject — insect, flower, texture, product, abstract

  • Define the lighting — softbox, ring light, natural diffused, backlight

  • Mention the surface — wet, polished, fibrous, crystalline

  • Use macro-specific terms — micro detail, shallow depth of field, bokeh, focus stacked

  • Request camera/lens — 100mm macro, f/2.8, 1:1 magnification

  • Add atmospheric effects — dust motes, water droplets, haze

  • Reference film stock — Kodak Portra, Velvia, black & white

❌ Avoid:

  • Flat, even lighting without texture emphasis

  • Overexposed or underexposed images without purpose

  • Wide shots or environmental scenes (unless combined with macro elements)

  • Crowded, chaotic compositions without a clear focal point

  • Forgetting to specify surface types for reflections

  • Overloading with too many subjects — keep it focused on one

  • Using the trigger string at the end of the prompt (always at the beginning)

What This LoRA Excels At

✅ Micro textures – skin, hair, scales, fibres, grains
✅ Insects & arachnids – compound eyes, wings, hairs
✅ Botanical macro – petals, stamens, pollen, dew
✅ Water droplets – refraction, caustics, condensation
✅ Iridescence – bubbles, beetles, oil slicks
✅ Product macro – jewellery, watches, electronics
✅ Abstract macro – fluids, patterns, light
✅ Scientific macro – focus-stacked, lab precision
✅ Shallow depth of field – creamy bokeh, subject isolation
✅ High detail – sharp focus, micro-contrast
✅ Natural light – soft, diffused, organic
✅ Studio lighting – controlled, even, product-ready
✅ Dark background – high contrast, subject pop
✅ Crystalline structures – snowflakes, salt, sugar
✅ Textures – wood, stone, metal, fabric

What This LoRA Does NOT Excel At

❌ Wide landscapes – this LoRA is for close-ups, not vistas
❌ Full-body portraits – unless the focus is on a macro detail (eye, skin)
❌ Action scenes – macro is about stillness and detail
❌ Cartoon, anime, or stylized illustration – keep it photographic
❌ Flat, even lighting – this LoRA thrives on texture and depth
❌ Bright, cheerful, comedy scenes – it prefers detailed, often moody atmospheres
❌ Modern or futuristic technology – unless it's a product macro
❌ Crowded street markets – without a clear macro subject
❌ Extreme weather – it does atmospheric effects, not chaos
❌ Purely naturalistic scenes – without a strong macro subject

Limitations & Notes for Krea 2

⚠️ Depth of field can be tricky – if the subject is too blurry, add sharp focus or reduce shallow depth of field.

⚠️ Complex scenes with more than 2 subjects may dilute the macro focus — prioritize 1 subject for maximum detail.

⚠️ Bokeh intensity can be controlled with: creamy bokeh, soft bokeh, busy bokeh, smooth background.

⚠️ Surface detail is key – always specify wet, polished, aged, weathered, or ornate.

⚠️ The negative prompt is essential – always exclude blurry, out of focus, flat lighting to maintain the signature aesthetic.

⚠️ (Macro:1.1) should always be at the very beginning of your prompt for maximum effect — moving it elsewhere reduces its influence.

⚠️ Facial expressions can lean towards neutral — use specific emotional descriptors or place figures in silhouette/distance.

V67 Macro celebrates the hidden world of the very small — where textures become landscapes, droplets become lenses, and every hair, scale, and fibre tells a story. Inspired by:

Cuties, it's close to the anniversary of when I first started seriously working with AI, so I wanted to make my first LoRA! ✺◟( ˃ᴗ˂ )◞✺ aww yiss!

💪 The LoRAs themselves work excellently between .4 - .6 weight, though I found my best results at between .48 - .52, favoring the later .52 if I'm running just one pass/single LoRA.

⚠️⚠️⚠️ KNOWN ISSUES:

These LoRAs were trained off of images that do not have good hands and feet! I was still learning when I genned the images, and the detailed hands and feet are few and far between! I did my best, but you will likely have to roll a few gens and seed combinations! You could also try prompting more, but I have not tried that!

😇 THIS LORA IS SFW. It does not include any nudity in it's training images!

👀👀👀 Detailed tagging and prompting guide, training images, training captions, and ComfyUI workflow included in the training data .zip!

I used Musubi Tuner to make a Z-Image LoRA using some of my first ever AI generations from early 2025! The 32 training images were made in January 2025 using Wai-Illustrious version 8 and Automatic1111, and the LoRA was made in December 2025! I used my customized Chat GPT 5.2 to write the base captions, and then I engineered and iterated upon them with Z-Image and the alpha-test LoRA to fine tune the training! I also increased the steps up to 480, and made 2 different versions using different VAE training! The AE version uses the base Z-Image ae.safetensor for the training, and the UltraFLUX uses a community modded vision version of the Flux VAE. I then created a customized workflow based on my observations during image testing!
